page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-8GB is a Starter family virtual server configured with 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, running on the KVM hypervisor. The processing power is delivered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. This configuration features 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core and utilizes a shared CPU allocation model. The server includes 40 GB of local SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show a significant variance between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier status in single-core CPU performance via stress-ng, as well as in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core performance is average, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the weak category. Memory bandwidth remains average for both small and large block reads and writes, while PassMark memory and database operation scores are weak.

Given its shared CPU allocation and Starter classification, this server offers resource density suitable for entry-level workloads. The primary tradeoff is the drop in performance when transitioning from single-threaded to multi-threaded operations, alongside weak database and Redis SET performance. Consequently, this server is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic application hosting, and single-threaded processing tasks, rather than intensive database management or multi-threaded computing.
